In [[knot theory]], a '''knot move''' or '''operation''' is a change or changes which preserve [[crossing number (knot theory)|crossing number]].<ref name="MW">{{Mathworld|KnotMove|Knot Move}}</ref> Operations are used to investigate whether knots are equivalent, [[prime knot|prime]] or [[nugatory crossing|reduced]].

Knot moves or operations include the [[flype]], [[Clasper (mathematics)#Cn-equivalence|Habiro move]], '''Markov moves''' (I. conjugation and II. stabilization), [[Arf invariant of a knot#Definition by pass equivalence|pass move]], [[Perko pair|Perko move]], and [[Reidemeister move]]s (I. twist move, II. poke move, and III. slide move).<ref name="MW"/>
